A1.justification: Both PDFs describe YEAST and are readable throughout, including equations, tables, figures and appendices. The substantial restructuring and changes in experimental coverage can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic simulations, private-platform data analyses and two deployment case studies in Sections 5–7, plus discrete-monitoring experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 reports original Online Retail semi-synthetic experiments in Section 4 and synthetic, sensitivity, discrete-monitoring and sample-saving results in Appendices B–D.

M1.justification: The fixed-boundary YEAST algorithm remains unchanged. However, v2 removes the progressive-threshold pYEAST procedure and Algorithm 2, together with the unequal-group and multiple-treatment adaptations from v1 Section 4. This substantially narrows the proposed method family.

E1.justification: V1's private-platform checkout data and two live A/B experiments are replaced by the public UK Online Retail dataset and semi-synthetic revenue interventions. The Gaussian, Student's t and Gamma simulations remain, relocated to Appendix B.

E2.justification: V2 adds LanDeMetsOBF and SeqC2ST-QDA to continuous-monitoring comparisons and a non-sequential t-test to the real-data power comparison. CAA disappears from reported comparisons. The discrete-monitoring tables also remove mSPRT, GAVI and Bonferroni comparisons that appeared in v1 Appendix B.

E3.justification: The reported real-data design changes from rolling two-week calibration and validation periods to six months for calibration and six months for validation. V2 adds artificial order-value reductions, input-misestimation controls, a GAVI parameter setting of 10,000, and a 100-checkpoint, piecewise-constant GST boundary for the public-data experiment. The retained basic synthetic simulation settings are largely unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds sensitivity tests that underestimate or overestimate N times V_N by 10% and 20% (Appendix B, Table 4 and Figure 1). It removes the pYEAST comparisons concerning threshold progression and period count, and both deployment case studies. Non-normal-distribution tests and robust-versus-non-robust variance comparisons remain.

E5.justification: V1 explicitly omits its calculated real-data confidence intervals; v2 displays intervals in Tables 2–3 and specifies Bonferroni correction for Table 2. V2 also documents seeds distributed across 13 processes. The reported aggregate replication count remains 100,000, so this does not establish an increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Under the retained normal-simulation setting, YEAST power at effect size 0.1 changes from 0.44 to 0.45 (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 4). V2 adds public-data power results, input-misestimation results and new comparator results, while removing pYEAST and deployment outcomes. For example, v2 Table 3 reports YEAST power of 0.678 at a 20% order-value reduction. The replacement real-data results use different reported data and protocols and cannot establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 removes the independence assumption and progressive-threshold derivation from v1 Section 4.2. Theorem 2 narrows the assumption from varying positive means E[X_i] = mu_i to a common positive mean, with corresponding proof revisions. V2 also derives an error-rate bound for multiplicative misestimation of N times V_N. The central Levy-inequality lemmas remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: V1 prominently claims a tuning-free procedure and theory that cannot be viewed as an extension of existing frameworks. V2 drops those headline claims, explicitly presents an asymptotic test, acknowledges a generalization of Miller's approach, and replaces the abstract's deployment claim with semi-synthetic validation. Unlimited monitoring and support for real-valued metrics remain core claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds explicit qualifications about estimating the finite horizon and variance, explains when alternative methods may be preferable, and interprets input-estimation errors quantitatively. It also explains the computational distinction from GST and the power comparison with a fixed-sample t-test. The central limitations concerning sensitivity to distributional changes without mean changes remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 supplies an identifiable public dataset source, date restrictions, missing-customer filtering and a concrete order count. It adds parallel-execution details, a reported 15-minute runtime on an Apple M3 Pro with 18 GB RAM, and implementation choices for the new baselines. These materially expand reproducibility information for the main empirical study. The same code companion remains cited.

R1.justification: V2 expands related work to e-processes and testing by betting, including new references on safe testing and sequential predictive tests. It revises the GST discussion to acknowledge potentially continuous monitoring and adds Section 2.3 positioning YEAST as a nontrivial generalization of Miller's test. This substantially changes the account of prior work and novelty.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, related work and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Synthetic experiments move from the main text to Appendix B, discrete monitoring becomes Appendix C, and sample savings receive Appendix D. Input-setting and formal-statement sections are reorganized under Section 3.3, and references move after the appendices.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column ACM layout to a single-column layout. Figure 1 is redrawn with side-by-side panels, revised axes and a different legend; the deployment Figure 2 is removed. V2 adds a real-data power table, displays uncertainty in the main result tables, and substantially restructures and relocates other tables.

improvement.justification: The public-data study reduces the reproducibility barrier of v1's private-data validation. Added baselines, explicit confidence intervals and input-error tests make the retained method's evidence easier to assess, while revised novelty and finite-horizon qualifications improve precision. Removing pYEAST, deployment cases and several discrete comparisons reduces practical breadth, but the stronger documentation and qualification of the core test support a limited net improvement.
